   Dubai’s inflation rate is likely to rise again in October after easing to 5.0% in September from 5.5% in August, Emirates NBD Research says. The decline largely reflected a sharp fall in volatile recreation and culture prices rather than a broad easing in price pressures, economist Daniel Richards says. Recreation and culture prices fell 13.8% on month and 8.2% on year, while food, housing and transport costs remained elevated. Higher petrol prices are expected to push inflation up again, with Emirates NBD forecasting the annual rate at around 5.6% by the end of 2026. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)

This is one factor behind the exchange’s push of its beef trims contract, which launched in July. Players who haven’t traditionally been involved with agricultural futures now find themselves attempting to hedge risk using CME futures. Ricci says this is true for those in the meat packing and distribution industries, as well as energy companies in the case of corn or sorghum contracts. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)

AL DRAGO/BLOOMBERG NEWS
 

There is room to assess economic developments before taking further monetary policy action, said Michelle Bowman, the Federal Reserve’s vice chair of supervision.

 

Speaking at the IIF Annual Membership Summit in Bangkok, Bowman briefly touched on her macroeconomic outlook before delving into her approach to financial regulation.

 

“Inflation remains above our goal,” she said Wednesday, but added that she doesn’t feel a sense of urgency to act in the wake of the last rate hike. “We have some time to wait and see how financial conditions evolve before we take more action.”

 

Earlier this month, Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said officials may need more time before deciding whether to raise rates again. New York Fed President John Williams has said there is “no need for urgency” after the Fed’s rate increase in September, but that it may be appropriate to hike once more this year.

From Dow Jones Newswires

 

Dubai’s inflation rate is likely to rise again in October after easing to 5.0% in September from 5.5% in August, Emirates NBD Research says. The decline largely reflected a sharp fall in volatile recreation and culture prices rather than a broad easing in price pressures, economist Daniel Richards says. Recreation and culture prices fell 13.8% on month and 8.2% on year, while food, housing and transport costs remained elevated. Higher petrol prices are expected to push inflation up again, with Emirates NBD forecasting the annual rate at around 5.6% by the end of 2026. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)

 

The volatility of macroeconomics this year has made hedging using agricultural futures contracts more attractive for traders, says John Ricci, Global Head of Agricultural Products for the CME Group. “We’re seeing things right now that we’ve not experienced before, and a lot of them are happening, unfortunately, at the same time,” Ricci told the WSJ. This is one factor behind the exchange’s push of its beef trims contract, which launched in July. Players who haven’t traditionally been involved with agricultural futures now find themselves attempting to hedge risk using CME futures. Ricci says this is true for those in the meat packing and distribution industries, as well as energy companies in the case of corn or sorghum contracts. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
